Olive Sourdough Baker's Percentage

Fold chopped olives in after the dough already has some strength, so the pieces stay chunky instead of smearing.

Detailed method

One round with olives folded in after the dough has some strength. Currently 500 g flour, 72% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 360 g water, 100 g starter, 10 g salt, 970 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 74.5% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 970 g. The olives are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 360 g water, the 100 g starter and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains. Leave the olives out. At 72% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Olives Cover the dough at about 24°C (75°F). After the first fold, about 30 minutes in, fold in 100 g of pitted, chopped olives, 20% of the flour. Give it two more folds over the next hour. The olives are extra and are not in the gram total. The dough is ready when it has grown by about half, about 3 to 4 hours from the mix.
  4. Shape Tip out 970 g of dough plus 100 g of olives and tighten them into one round, without smearing the olives. This batch is 1 loaf. The default batch is 970 g of dough plus 100 g of olives, in a round lidded pot about 24 cm across and 11 cm high. If you change the amount, use a pot sized to fit, or split the dough.
  5. Proof Cover it for 45 to 70 minutes, until it looks puffy. With 20% starter, bake it if the top starts to sink.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the lidded pot inside. Place the dough on parchment and lower it, paper and all, into the hot pot. Score once. Bake 20 minutes covered, then 16 to 22 minutes uncovered, until the crust is golden and the olives on the surface look set. If you have no lid, invert another pot or a deep tray over the loaf for the first 20 minutes. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
